ethics_check.report:
Based on the following text, we would expect an ethics approval statement, and it was present:

> Overall, 28/44 (63.6%) of these PMBB participants had a personal history of at least one malignancy, including 39 solid malignant neoplasms (13 types), and five hematologic malignancies (two types) (Supplementary Tables 4, 5).

> In the PMBB cohort, we found that 9.1% of participants had bronchus/lung cancer with an average age of diagnosis of 64.2 years (SD=12.0, range 47-75) earlier the United States population average age of diagnosis of 70 years. 41 Four of four PMBB participants with NSCLC had a history of smoking.

Ethics approval statement:

> This study was carried out under IRB protocol 832122.

> UKBB participants with POT1 variants were ascertained from a population-based cohort study of 469,558 participants with whole exome sequencing (UKBB projects 69929, 54389) with linkage to electronic health records and the UK National Cancer Registration and Analysis Service (NCRAS). 31 The UKBB is approved by the UK Biobank Research Ethics Committee.

> Chart review was carried out under IRB protocol 854086.

> Ethics Declaration: This study was approved by the University of Pennsylvania IRB, protocol #813913.

> Geisinger data was collected and analyzed under the Geisinger IRB approved protocol #2021-0818.

power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

stat_p_nonsig.report: Meta-scientific research has shown nonsignificant p values are commonly misinterpreted. It is incorrect to infer that there is 'no effect', 'no difference', or that groups are 'the same' after p > 0.05. It is possible that there is a true non-zero effect, but that the study did not detect it. Make sure your inference acknowledges that it is possible that there is a non-zero effect. It is correct to include the effect is 'not significantly' different, although this just restates that p > 0.05. Metacheck does not yet analyze automatically whether sentences which include non-significant p-values are correct, but we recommend manually checking the sentences below for possible misinterpreted non-significant p values. ```{r} #| echo: false # table data -------------------------------------- table <- structure(list(Text = c("p=0.059", "p=0.08", "p=0.66"), Sentence = c("Urinary tract cancers were significantly associated with POT1 variant carrier status (OR 3.05, 95% CI 1.20-7.76, p=0.031), and bronchus and lung cancers were no longer significantly associated with carrier status (OR 2.90, 95% CI 1.04-8.11, p=0.059) (Supplementary Table 3).", "The average age of earliest cancer diagnosis was 50.5 (SD=13.1, range 29-68) for the clinical cohort compared to 56.6 (SD=12.1, range 26-79) for the PMBB cohort (p=0.08) (Figure 2; Supplementary Table 6).", "those without (p=0.66, Figure 4), which may be age-related as individuals with cancer were significantly older (p=2.25x10 -11 )." )), row.names = c(NA, -3L), class = c("tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame" )) # display table ----------------------------------- metacheck::report_table(table, c(0.1, 0.9), 10, FALSE) ``` ::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"} For metascientific articles demonstrating the rate of misinterpretations of non-significant results is high, see: Aczel B, Palfi B, Szollosi A, Kovacs M, Szaszi B, Szecsi P, Zrubka M, Gronau Q, van den Bergh D, Wagenmakers E (2018). “Quantifying Support for the Null Hypothesis in Psychology: An Empirical Investigation.” Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science, 1(3), 357–366. doi:10.1177/2515245918773742. Murphy S, Merz R, Reimann L, Fernández A (2025). “Nonsignificance misinterpreted as an effect’s absence in psychology: Prevalence and temporal analyses.” Royal Society Open Science, 12(3), 242167. doi:10.1098/rsos.242167. For educational material on preventing the misinterpretation of p values, see [Improving Your Statistical Inferences](https://lakens.github.io/statistical_inferences/01-pvalue.html#sec-misconception1). :::

UKBB participants with POT1 variants were ascertained from a population-based cohort study of 469,558 participants with whole exome sequencing (UKBB projects 69929, 54389) with linkage to electronic health records and the UK National Cancer Registration and Analysis Service (NCRAS). 31 The UKBB is approved by the UK Biobank Research Ethics Committee.

live_data_statements: Overall, 28/44 (63.6%) of these PMBB participants had a personal history of at least one malignancy, including 39 solid malignant neoplasms (13 types), and five hematologic malignancies (two types) (Supplementary Tables 4, 5).

In the PMBB cohort, we found that 9.1% of participants had bronchus/lung cancer with an average age of diagnosis of 64.2 years (SD=12.0, range 47-75) earlier the United States population average age of diagnosis of 70 years. 41 Four of four PMBB participants with NSCLC had a history of smoking.
